newsitem.title: USA: US names possible Beaufort Sea lease sale area.
newsitem.headline: US names possible Beaufort Sea lease sale area.

text.p: The U.S. Minerals Management Service Wednesday said 1.7 million acres will be studied for possible inclusion in the next federal Outer Continental Shelf lease sale for the Beaufort Sea, tentatively set for early April 1998.
The area includes 363 blocks, and is located three to 25 miles off Alaska's arctic coast. Water depths in the area range from 25 to 120 feet, the MMS said.
The area under consideration focuses on near shore blocks from the east of the Colville River to west of Barter Island.
A draft environmental impact statement on potential effects of leasing in that area is to be issued in May, and a decision whether to issue a notice of sale is to be made in early 1998, the MMS said.
There have been six federal sales conducted in the Beaufort since 1979. The MMS has issued 660 leases there, and 78 remain as active leases.
The MMS said 28 exploratory wells have been drilled, and nine leases were determined to be producible, but none was considered economically feasible.
The last Beaufort lease sale was held September 1996.
